clue.text: Memorial day, you intended to say

indicators.note: what you would say out loud is wanted, so the spoken phrase stands in for its spelling

blocks.note: MON is the short form of Monday
'you meant' said out loud, respelt as a word ending

explanation.surface: Someone on a remembrance day corrects what they were trying to say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Memorial day' reads as one phrase, the US holiday, but the definition stops at 'Memorial'.
explanation.definitionFit: A monument is a structure built to commemorate a person or event, which is what a memorial is.

clue.text: Rising opera company produces single

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters are read from the bottom upwards

blocks.note: English National Opera

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming opera company puts out a single record.
explanation.definitionFit: One is a single unit; both words mean a lone item.

clue.text: Writer dipping into funds occasionally for turnover?

definitions.note: the answer is a verb; the question mark lets the noun-looking 'turnover' be read as 'turn over'

indicators.note: occasionally means only now and then, so just every other letter of the word is kept
something dipping into another goes inside it, so one piece sits within the other

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of funds
a pen is a writing implement

explanation.surface: An author borrows from savings now and then to keep the business turning over.
explanation.definitionFit: To upend something is to turn it over or set it on its end.

clue.text: Flower in field regularly surrounded by wind

indicators.note: regularly means at fixed intervals, so letters are taken at evenly spaced positions
one piece is surrounded by another, so it is placed inside it

blocks.note: second and fourth letters of field
an easterly is a wind from the east

explanation.surface: A bloom in a meadow is buffeted by the wind.
explanation.definitionFit: The Easter lily is a white trumpet-shaped lily associated with Easter.

clue.text: Final song by Jim Morrison's group?

blocks.note: first meaning: the conclusion
second meaning: a 1967 track by the Doors, fronted by Jim Morrison

explanation.walkthrough: Jim Morrison sang for the Doors, whose famous long track closes their first album. It is also a theme answer: a Fourth Plinth sculpture of the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a finish or conclusion and the title of a well-known Doors song.

clue.text: Attacks oil company gaining the last in profits

indicators.note: the last in a word is its final letter, so only the closing letter is kept

blocks.note: Shell is a major oil company
final letter of profits

explanation.surface: Critics lay into an oil giant as it posts big profits.
explanation.definitionFit: To shell is to bombard with artillery, so shells is a verb meaning attacks.

clue.text: Send head of security in

indicators.note: the head of a word is its front, so only its opening letter is kept

blocks.note: first letter of security
hip means fashionable, as does in

explanation.surface: An order to dispatch the chief of security inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To ship goods is to dispatch them, so ship is a synonym for send.

clue.text: Festival buys Glastonbury ultimately with master's payment plan

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter is kept
a festival that buys something takes it in, so the piece goes inside

blocks.note: Easter is a Christian festival
last letter of Glastonbury
M for master, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: A music festival snaps up Glastonbury with a head's instalment plan.
explanation.walkthrough: Glastonbury is a famous English music festival, which makes 'Festival' look like it means that one; it is Easter.
explanation.definitionFit: Easy terms are an arrangement to pay in instalments, a kind of payment plan.

clue.text: Flying solo over Spain to transfer money

indicators.note: letters that are flying are scattered through the air and land in a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
E is the international vehicle code for Spain
to change is to switch over or transfer

explanation.surface: A lone pilot crossing Spain wires funds abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' places the first piece before Spain's letter in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Loose change is small coins carried in a pocket, a form of money.

clue.text: Just during the weekend game of rugby

indicators.note: something happening during a period falls inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: Saturday and Sunday, abbreviated S and S
just and even both mean fair

explanation.surface: Only on Saturday or Sunday is there a rugby match.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevens is the seven-a-side version of rugby union, a short fast form of the game.

clue.text: Issue action on the internet?

blocks.note: the E- prefix of email and e-commerce marks things online
a mission is an operation or action

explanation.surface: A call to take an online campaign further.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the invented word e-mission, an action done online.
explanation.definitionFit: An emission is something given off or issued, so the noun issue fits it.

clue.text: Britain's unfortunately long used to strikes

indicators.note: things that turn out unfortunately go wrong, so these letters are knocked out of order

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for Britain
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumble that Britain has long been used to industrial action.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strikes' looks like walkouts but is a verb: hits.
explanation.definitionFit: To bludgeon is to hit hard with a heavy club, so bludgeons means strikes.

clue.text: A believer in free will is an irritable fool!

indicators.note: to fool with something is to mess about with it, so the letters get muddled

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A grumpy verdict that anyone believing in free will is a cranky idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fool' reads as a noun insult, but it works as the verb, to mess about.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy a libertarian holds that people have free will, as opposed to a determinist.

clue.text: Different? Or what two relations have in common

definitions.text: what two relations have in common

blocks.note: first meaning: not the same

blocks.clueFragment: what two relations have in common
blocks.note: second meaning: the letter string shared by the words for a female parent and a male sibling

explanation.walkthrough: The relations are mother and brother, both ending in the same five letters. It is also a theme answer: One & Other was Antony Gormley's Fourth Plinth project.
explanation.definitionFit: Other means distinct or not the same, so it can replace the adjective different.

clue.text: Supervisor's requirement to play bridge, say?

indicators.note: say asks for what is heard when spoken, not what is written

blocks.note: bridge is a card game for four players

explanation.surface: A boss's prerequisite for a game of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', joining the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A foreperson is the person in charge of a group of workers, a supervisor.

clue.text: Courage felt to be shown in recession

indicators.note: the answer is shown sitting inside the words in front of it
something in recession goes backwards, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: running across the words from the end back to the start

explanation.surface: Bravery is needed during an economic downturn.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for nerve or courage.
explanation.definitionFit: In British informal speech, bottle means nerve or courage, as in 'lose your bottle'.

clue.text: Rising artist's skill covering wrong flag in battle

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading from the bottom upwards
letters set out wrong are in the wrong order and need rearranging
one piece covering another wraps around it

blocks.note: RA, Royal Academician, a crossword artist; the 's is possessive
art is a skill or craft
taken as written

explanation.surface: An up-and-coming painter's knack involves a misjudged flag in a war scene.
explanation.walkthrough: Trafalgar, Nelson's 1805 naval victory, also names the London square with the Fourth Plinth, the puzzle's theme.
explanation.definitionFit: Trafalgar was a sea battle of 1805 between the British and Franco-Spanish fleets.

clue.text: United breaking out of position

indicators.note: something breaking into another splits it open and sits in the gap

blocks.note: forth means out or away, as in 'go forth'
U is the abbreviation for United in team names

explanation.surface: A football team breaking out of their league place.
explanation.walkthrough: Theme answer: the Fourth Plinth in Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: Fourth is a place in an order or ranking, so it names a position.

clue.text: Certainly join forces again?

blocks.note: first meaning: truly, indeed
second meaning: read as ..., to form an alliance once more

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits the second sense splits the word into RE (again) and ALLY (join forces).
explanation.definitionFit: Really is an adverb of emphasis meaning truly or certainly, and re-ally is an invented verb.

clue.text: Hold new Lemsip at first to stop runny nose

indicators.note: at first points to the opening letter of the word before it
something runny flows and loses its shape, so the letters lose their order
a stopper plugs a gap, so this piece goes into the middle of the other

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new
first letter of Lemsip
taken as written

explanation.surface: Advice to dose a streaming cold with Lemsip.
explanation.walkthrough: Lemsip is a British cold and flu remedy. The N goes in front; the L is plugged into the reshuffled nose after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A nelson is a wrestling hold applied by an arm under the opponent's armpit and hand on the neck.

clue.text: Top six in Premier League, including Newcastle, thank home support

indicators.note: the top of each of the next six words is its first letter

blocks.note: first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter
first letter

explanation.surface: Newcastle, now in the Premier League's top six, thanks its loyal home crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top six' looks like a league table position; it means the first letters of six words. Theme answer: the Fourth Plinth.
explanation.definitionFit: A plinth is the base block on which a statue or column stands, a support.

clue.text: Stories from Johannesburg's exciting event?

blocks.note: Johannesburg is in South Africa, SA
a gas is informal for something great fun

explanation.surface: Tales coming out of a thrilling occasion in Johannesburg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a gas' is informal for a lot of fun, so an exciting event.
explanation.definitionFit: Sagas are long stories, originally Norse heroic tales, now any long narrative.

clue.text: Everyone's powers drop 25% with abnormal reactions

indicators.note: dropping a quarter means losing a quarter of the word's letters

blocks.note: everyone is all; the 's is possessive
energies are powers or strengths

explanation.surface: Everybody's strength flags by a quarter when their body overreacts.
explanation.walkthrough: Eight letters lose a quarter, so the first two go.
explanation.definitionFit: Allergies are the immune system's abnormal reactions to substances such as pollen.

clue.text: Sticks with muscles, not bone

indicators.note: not means without, so the following piece is taken out

blocks.note: glutes are buttock muscles
T as in T-bone steak

explanation.surface: Holding together with flesh alone and no skeleton.
explanation.walkthrough: A T-bone is a steak, so 'bone' gives the letter T.
explanation.definitionFit: To glue is to stick things together, so glues is a verb meaning sticks.

blocks.note: G, a grand, is slang for a thousand pounds
the two zeros read as letters
D is the Roman numeral for 500

explanation.surface: A large sum of money, and the speaker is pleased.
explanation.walkthrough: The long number splits into £1000, 00 and 500.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something 'ain't bad' is a casual way of calling it good.

clue.text: Ruler once capturing Major without volunteers

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the following piece is removed

blocks.note: capturing a piece in chess is taking it
the TA, Territorial Army, was Britain's volunteer reserve
John Major, UK prime minister 1990-97

explanation.surface: A former monarch takes an army major prisoner without any volunteers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Major' looks like a rank; it is the surname of a British prime minister, whose first name is wanted.
explanation.definitionFit: King John ruled England from 1199 to 1216 and sealed Magna Carta.

clue.text: Settle2

blocks.note: first meaning: to pay off, as in squaring a debt
second meaning: the superscript 2 printed after the word means multiplied by itself

explanation.walkthrough: The 2 is a superscript, the mathematical sign for raising a number to the second power. Theme answer: Trafalgar Square.
explanation.definitionFit: To square an account is to settle it, and the superscript 2 is read as 'square' or 'squared'.

clue.text: Peculiar drink

blocks.note: first meaning: odd, in old-fashioned British slang
second meaning: a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.walkthrough: Rum as an adjective is dated British for strange, as in 'a rum business'.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both dated slang for odd and the name of a spirit made from sugar cane.

clue.text: Answer back communist to get caught

indicators.note: back means going the other way, so the letters are read right to left

blocks.note: ANS is the abbreviation for answer
a Red is a communist

explanation.surface: A communist retorts and ends up arrested.
explanation.definitionFit: Snared means trapped or caught, as an animal in a snare.

clue.text: Large cab carrying 500 east

indicators.note: a vehicle carrying something holds it inside

blocks.note: a hansom is a horse-drawn cab
D is the Roman numeral for 500
E for east

explanation.surface: A big taxi carries 500 passengers eastward.
explanation.walkthrough: Handsome is used here as in 'a handsome sum'.
explanation.definitionFit: A handsome amount is a generous or large one, so the adjective means large.
